en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Third Chapter
The Discussion on the Eighth-Stage Person: Is the obsession with views abandoned by the eighth-stage person? Yes.

"Is it to be said that the person who is an eighth-rank attainer (aṭṭhamaka) dwells having entered upon, attained, acquired, reached, and realized the fruit of stream-entry (sotāpatti), dwelling having touched it with the body?
No, it should not be so stated... [etc.
...Is doubt-obsession abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank attainer?"
“Yes,” you say.
“Is the person who is an eighth-rank individual a stream-enterer who has attained the fruit of stream-entry …pe… and dwells having touched it with his body?
You must not say so …pe….
Is the obsession of views abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner?
Yes. Is the underlying tendency to views abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the obsession of views abandoned by a person who is an eighth-rank individual? Yes.
Is the underlying tendency to doubt and the adherence to rites and rituals abandoned by the person who is at the eighth stage?
One should not say so... [as before] ...
Is the obsession by doubt abandoned by the person who is at the eighth stage?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then has the underlying tendency to doubt been abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is the obsession of doubt abandoned by a person who is at the eighth stage? Yes.
Is the underlying tendency to views... the adherence to rules and observances abandoned by a person who is at the eighth stage?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency to views unabandoned in the person who has reached the eighth stage? Yes.
Is the obsession of views (*diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhāna*) not yet abandoned by the person who is a "candidate for the first fruit" (*aṭṭhamaka*)?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...is the underlying tendency of views (*diṭṭhānusaya*) not yet abandoned by the person who is a "candidate for the first fruit"?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is the obsession of doubt not yet abandoned by a person who is at the stage of the eighth person?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is the underlying tendency to doubt and the adherence to rules and observances unabandoned in the person who is an eighth-rank individual?
Yes. Is the obsession by wrong view unabandoned in the person who is an eighth-rank individual?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*) unabandoned by a person who is an eighth-rank practitioner (*aṭṭhamaka*)? Yes.
Is the obsession of doubt not yet abandoned by the person who is at the stage of the eighth?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is the obsession of wrong view abandoned by the person who is at the stage of the eighth?
“Yes,” you say.
“Has the path been developed by the person in the eighth stage for the abandoning of the obsession of views?
You should not speak thus … [as before] … No, indeed.
Is the obsession of views abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank individual?

Yes. Are the foundations of mindfulness developed for the abandoning of the obsession of views by the person who is an eighth-rank individual? ... [and so on] ... are the right efforts ... [and so on] ... are the factors of enlightenment developed?
It should not be said so.
Is the obsession of doubt abandoned by a person who is an eighth-rank individual? Yes.

Is it not the case that for the person who is an *aṭṭhamaka* (the eighth person), the path has been cultivated for the abandoning of the obsession of doubt … [and] the factors of awakening have been cultivated?
One should not say so … [as before].
Has the path not been cultivated by the person who is an *aṭṭhamaka* for the abandoning of the obsession of views?
“Yes,” you say.
“But has it been abandoned by a path that is mundane, with taints, and subject to defilement?
You must not say so … [and so on] … No, indeed.

Is it the case that for the eighth person, the foundations of mindfulness, the [right] exertions, the bases of power, the faculties, the powers, the factors of enlightenment, and the Noble Eightfold Path have not been developed for the sake of abandoning the obsession of views?
Yes. Is that which has been abandoned by a path that is mundane, with taints, and subject to defilement [abandoned]? Yes.

It should not be said thus … [as before] … Has the path for the abandoning of the obsession of doubt not been cultivated by the person who is at the eighth stage … [and so on] … have the foundations of mindfulness … [and so on] … the factors of enlightenment not been cultivated?
Yes.
Is it abandoned by a path that is mundane, with taints, and subject to defilement?
One should not say so... [and so on]...
One should not say this.
“Is the obsession of views abandoned by the person who has reached the eighth stage?”—
Yes. “Will it arise again?”— No.
It will not arise.
If it will not arise, then indeed, sir, you must say:
"The obsession of views has been abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner."
Is it not to be said that “the obsession by doubt has been abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner”?
Yes, it is.
"Will it arise? "It will not arise.
If it will not arise, then indeed, my dear sir, you must say:
“The obsession of doubt has been abandoned by the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner.
Is it because the obsession of wrong view will not arise in the person who is an eighth-rank practitioner that it is said to have been abandoned?
Yes.
Is it because one considers that the underlying tendency to views will not arise in the person at the stage of the eighth (the *aṭṭhamaka*) that it is said to have been abandoned?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is it because one considers that the obsession by views will not arise in the person at the stage of the eighth that it is said to have been abandoned?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Since it is held that for a person who is an eighth-rank practitioner (*aṭṭhamaka*), the underlying tendency to doubt (*vicikicchānusaya*) ... and the misapprehension of rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*) will not arise, it has therefore been abandoned?
One should not speak thus... [and so on].
Is it because the obsession of doubt will not arise in the person who has reached the eighth stage that it is said to be abandoned?
Yes. Is it because the underlying tendency to doubt … the adherence to rules and observances will not arise in the person who has reached the eighth stage that it is said to be abandoned? Yes.
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is it because one considers that the obsession of views will not arise in a person who has entered the eighth stage that it is said to be abandoned?
Yes.
Is it because one considers that the obsession of views will not arise for a person who is a "lineage-holder" (gotrabhū) that it is said to be abandoned?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is it because one considers that the obsession of doubt will not arise for a person who is a "eighth-person" (aṭṭhamaka) that it is said to be abandoned?
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is it because one considers that for a person who has entered the lineage (gotrabhū), the obsession of doubt will not arise, that it is therefore abandoned?
“One should not say so,” … [and so on].
The Discussion on the Eighth-Ranked One is finished.
